adjudication.evidence: Original N/E/U shows a sustained negative N shift (~-8 to -12 mm) and positive E shift (~4 to 10 mm) from ~day 637 to ~day 670, followed by a return toward prior levels by day 676. P1 (637–670) aligns with this full offset-return pattern in N and E; interior points (e.g., day 650–660) remain offset, supporting a genuine temporary platform. P2 (644–657) is fully embedded in P1 and lacks independent return; its onset/offset are not distinct from P1’s trend. P3 (661–692) begins after P1’s return starts and overlaps with a large negative U jump at ~day 676 (visible in original: U drops from ~1.3 to ~-18.6), but the N/E behavior during P3 does not show a coherent offset-return—N/E continue drifting post-P1 without reversal. P4 (676–695) coincides with the large U step and subsequent recovery, but N/E do not exhibit a matching offset-return; instead, they resume pre-P1 trend. P5 (686–687) is a single-point anomaly, not a platform. Only P1 satisfies the criteria: sustained shift on ≥2 axes followed by opposing return, with interior observations consistently offset. No other pair forms an independent temporary platform.
